title: ccp.config.yaml
description: The one file an organisation edits. Everything else in this repository is meant to work unchanged. Created by `ccp init`, checked by `ccp doctor`, and read by every collector. NO CREDENTIALS LIVE HERE - secrets come from environment variables, named in this file but never valued in it, so the config can be committed to your own repository without a secret-scanning incident.

affirming_official.description: The named person who affirms in SPRS. Recorded because the affirmation is a personal attestation with real exposure, not a system action - nothing in this tool ever performs it.

approach.description: The Phase 0 decision everything else follows from. `enclave` isolates CUI to a defined boundary and is the recommended default; `enterprise` puts the whole estate in scope and multiplies assessment cost, control count and SSP surface.

cloud_environment.description: GCC High and DoD tenants do NOT use graph.microsoft.com - they use graph.microsoft.us with a different login host. Getting this wrong is the most common reason a DIB tenant returns 401 against code that works fine in commercial.

break_glass_attribute.description: The user attribute marking a break-glass account. An attribute, never a name pattern: a naming convention is not an access control, and matching on one means the population silently changes when somebody renames an account.

phishing_resistant_methods.description: Which registered methods count as phishing-resistant for this organisation. Configurable because the answer is a policy decision, not a fact.

org_url.description: Okta org URL, e.g. https://acme.okta.com or https://acme.okta-gov.com. Government orgs are on okta-gov.com and okta.mil - the same trap as graph.microsoft.us.

region.description: Primary region. AWS GovCloud is us-gov-west-1 or us-gov-east-1 - a commercial region here silently queries the wrong partition.

aggregator.description: AWS Config aggregator name. With one, a single query spans every declared account; without one, only the account the ambient credential belongs to is read - and the collector says so rather than implying it covered them all.

owner_tag.description: Tag key carrying the asset owner. Defaults to 'owner'. Real estates use Owner, owner, team, CostCenter - a hardcoded key silently reports every correctly-tagged resource as unowned.

classification_tag.description: Tag key carrying the data classification. Defaults to 'data_classification'.

max_staleness_days.description: How old the newest AWS Config item may be before the snapshot stops counting as current. Default 7. A recorder can be running and capturing nothing; item age is the only signal that separates a quiet account from a broken pipeline.

cmdb.description: The asset system of record - what the organisation believes is in the boundary. Separate from cloud on purpose: the asset control reconciles this against what the cloud actually reports, and one setting driving both makes the two halves mutually exclusive.

mdm.description: Managed endpoints enrolled in the enclave. Absent from both the CMDB and the cloud API, and the asset class most likely to hold an opened CUI document.

entity_list_1260h_path.description: A CSV of the current published Section 1260H list. This repository does NOT ship the list - it changes on a recurring cadence and a stale copy is worse than none, because a supplier screened against it reads as screened.

engine.description: duckdb runs locally with no server and no Python, which is what makes this repository runnable on a laptop the day you clone it. The SQL models stay dbt-compatible, so a real warehouse is a migration rather than a rewrite.

retain_days.description: MINIMUM retention: a commitment to keep at least this much evidence history, the way retention periods read elsewhere in this domain. It is NOT a delete-after trigger and nothing in this tool deletes evidence. Read as a ceiling it would be harmful: firstObserved walks history backwards to the last passing snapshot, so dropping the oldest snapshots silently shortens every open variance episode - a subject failing across 600 days of monthly snapshots reports 180 days once pruned to a 180-day window, understating Variance Duration by 70% in the direction that flatters the control. ccp doctor reports the span actually held against this number.

fixture_path.description: Where --fixture runs write. Defaults to a `fixture/` subdirectory of evidence.path, and should almost never be set. Synthetic and real evidence must not share a directory: a fixture run would overwrite that day's real assertion file, and prior-evidence reads would date real findings from synthetic snapshots. Pointing this at evidence.path is refused at write time.
